meta.name: PureScore questionnaire coverage audit — cumulative log
meta.lens: product-coverage (capture → score → wearable-match → persona → goals → nudge → adherence)

revisions.note: Baseline product-loop audit: loop scorecard, pillar/reservoir heatmaps, 6 findings, spec sketches.
Versioned/cumulative log; per-metric source tagging + per-pillar fusion scenarios; wearable cadence×provider matrix; metric-calculation popups.
Front-of-loop / onboarding pass: evaluated the first-run intake experience — added 4 stage-1 Capture findings (F9–F12) and an onboarding coverage matrix; Capture scorecard verdict revised ok→partial.

Closed the onboarding cluster (D26): built the Onboarding & first-run spec (steps, demographic field-set, question-side cold-start + progressive profiling, consent & device gating) — F9–F12 auto-verify.

Typed source channel per marker (D28): all 80 markers resolve to one of 6 channels via marker_channel(); surfaced in Appendix A + biomarkers grid; fusion rules now enforceable — F7 auto-verifies. Wearable-corroboration registry (D29): 23 wearable.* refs → 17 canonical metrics + tolerances; wearable-match stage typed — F4 auto-verifies.
Closed the last two P2s (D30): per-metric Freshness SLA beneath the cadence matrix (F8) and 6 HEP/REN symptom self-report items added to the bank (F5). All 12 findings now Addressed.

meta.status_rule: auto_rule may promote a stored status to 'addressed' when its expression is true against the live build stats; it never demotes.

versions.body: 0 adherence items in the bank. The loop cannot close: completed / partial / skipped nudges never re-enter as reservoir inflows (Doc 04) or move the engagement & Trajectory companion dimensions (Doc 12). Without it, personalization can't learn what works. Fix: the adherence micro check-in instrument (see sketch, Adherence sketch).

Built (D25): Appendix H ships 41 adherence micro check-ins (data/adherence.json), one per nudge family, each writing an adherence ∈ [0,1] value + reason back to its reservoir (Doc 04) and the engagement dimension (Doc 12). The loop now closes; adher_n > 0 so this auto-verifies.

Expanded (v4): Appendix H now ships 41 check-ins — 15 lifestyle + 20 medication + 6 disease-management — gated so only relevant ones fire: medication/disease items carry a coded ehr_trigger (ATC · ICD-10) that auto-activates from the Patient360 EHR graph (onboarding screener as fallback), with dose/event-anchored timing captured at onboarding. Covers the most frequent chronic meds/conditions (statins, metformin, SGLT2i/GLP-1, RAAS, beta-blockers, DOACs, levothyroxine, ICS/LABA, SSRIs, vit-D, iron, bisphosphonates, allopurinol, CPAP, CKD/HF routines…) with UAE-priority flags. adher_n > 0 still auto-verifies.

Personas are used to gate questions and frame ranges, but nothing lets the engine infer a persona/archetype from the answers (0 questions carry a persona-determination weight). Cold-start can't resolve a new user to a frame, so early scoring stays generic. Fix: a signal→persona weight matrix + softmax posterior (see Persona-matrix sketch).

Built (D25): Appendix I ships the determination matrix (data/persona-matrix.json): 37 personas (13 clinical × 24 archetype) × 36 signals with signed weights, hard sex/age/life-stage priors, and a softmax posterior so a persona is inferred from answers. persona_det_n > 0 auto-verifies.

The UserGoals stream (state machine) and goal-focused nudge re-ranking have no backing data; goals can't be bound to persona / lifestyle / age / sex / condition or scored for progress against a wearable/lab metric. Fix: a goals catalogue keyed by applicability (see Goals sketch).

Built (D25): Appendix J ships 32 goals (data/goals.json), ≥2 per pillar, each keyed by an applicability vector (persona · archetype · life-stage · age · sex · condition) with a wearable/lab/PRO target, modifiability, and linked Appendix-H nudges — driving the UserGoals lifecycle on the state machine. goal_struct > 0 auto-verifies.
corroborated_by is prose, not a typed link to a wearable metric, so stage-3 can't be automated or audited; a large share of questions have no actual to check perceived answers against.

Advanced by this revision: added (a) per-metric source-channel tags and per-pillar fusion scenarios (§ Source fusion) and (b) a metric × provider cadence matrix (§ Cadence). Remaining: typed question → wearable-metric → tolerance links inside the bank itself.

Built (D29): the Wearable corroboration registry (data/wearable-corroboration.json) types the wearable-match stage — all 23 of the bank's wearable.* refs normalize (casing/aliases collapsed) to 17 canonical metrics (Appendix B), each with a source channel and a tolerance (the perceived↔actual agreement band the gap engine applies). Surfaced as an appendix + filterable grid. wear_corr_typed > 0 auto-verifies.
HEP and REN get a small fraction of the self-report weight that INF / CV / MCS carry.

Documented as a deliberate design choice: both pillars are lab-led — the source-fusion table (§ Source fusion) shows biomarker-lab as the dominant channel for REN/HEP, with self-report contributing context/adherence only. Optional: add 2–3 symptom/risk self-report items each.

Built (D30): added 6 symptom/risk self-report items to the bank (data/qb-02-renal-hepatic.json → re-enriched) — REN: oedema/foamy-urine/fatigue, NSAID use, urination change; HEP: RUQ/jaundice symptoms, fatty-liver/hepatitis history, hepatotoxin exposure — each corroborated by the relevant lab. LIFE-stream HEP/REN coverage now 40/41. hep_ren_symptoms >= 6 auto-verifies.

Appendix D (clinical, 15) and Appendix F (lifestyle archetypes, 25) overlap but aren't a single comprehensive set, so 'all possible personas' is ambiguous and the determination matrix has no canonical target.
Resolved: the comprehensive persona set publishes the canonical union (13 clinical × 24 archetype = up to 37 frames) as the explicit determination target for the §-fusion / persona matrix.

items.title: Markers lack a typed source channel

versions.body: Surfaced by this revision's source-tagging pass: markers carry a free-text guideline source but no typed channel ({biomarker-lab · wearable-clinical · wearable-consumer · wearable-inferential · self-report · derived}), so the multi-source fusion rules (§ Source fusion) can't be enforced programmatically. Fix: add a channel enum per marker in the data model (Doc 01).

Built (D28): every marker now resolves to a typed source channel via marker_channel() in wiki_content.py — one of {biomarker-lab · wearable-clinical · wearable-consumer · wearable-inferential · self-report · derived}. Surfaced as the Channel column in Appendix A and as a filterable column on the biomarkers grid; the §-fusion rules are now programmatically enforceable. source_typed > 0 (80 markers) auto-verifies.

Surfaced by the cadence trace (§ Cadence): there is no freshness/cadence contract per provider, so the 'stale wearable' state (state machine) has no per-source threshold and the Confidence dimension can't decay correctly per metric. Fix: define a staleness window + expected cadence per metric × provider.

Built (D30): a per-metric Freshness SLA — expected cadence · fresh-within · stale-after · drives — added beneath the cadence matrix. It gives the Wearables → stale state a concrete per-metric threshold and lets Confidence decay correctly (Doc 12 §4). Provider determines delivery (matrix); the SLA is the clinical staleness bound. cadence_sla > 0 auto-verifies.

The word onboarding appears on 0 wiki pages. The question content is broad (validated PROs Appx C, the question bank Appx E, axes/archetypes Appx F) and persona/goals inference now exist (F2/F3), but no document owns the first-run experience: the sequence of demographic + lifestyle/PRO + goals + consent + device-pairing capture, what is asked when, and how the score bootstraps on day-0. Doc 18 describes effortless surfaces (scribe/chat/scheduling) and the 📝 LIFE / 🎯 GOAL streams; Doc 01 the data schema — neither narrates intake. Fix: an onboarding/intake spec (an owning doc, or a Doc 01/18 section) wiring the existing catalogue, persona matrix (Appx I) and goals (Appx J) into a first-run flow. See the onboarding coverage matrix.

Built (D26): Onboarding & first-run (data/onboarding.json) now owns the first-run experience — 11 ordered steps from welcome → consent → demographics → goal-seed → bootstrap PROs → persona resolution → device/EHR connect → first score → progressive profiling, wiring the question bank (Appx E), persona matrix (Appx I) and goals (Appx J) into one flow. onboarding_steps > 0 auto-verifies.

Patient(… sex_at_birth, gender_identity, dob, …) in Doc 01 §1.1 defines sex/gender/age but leaves the rest of the demographic field-set implicit (the trailing …). Ethnicity drives cohort stratification (NHANES, Doc 01 §4.2) and UAE cut-points (Doc 15) yet is never enumerated as a captured intake item; region/locale, occupation, language, household role are absent (occupation surfaces only in Appx F). The literal term demographic occurs on a single wiki page. Fix: enumerate the demographic intake set in Doc 01 with each field's use — physiology · stratification · localization · communication.

Built (D26): the demographic field-set is now enumerated (11 fields: sex-at-birth, gender, DOB, height, weight, ethnicity, ancestry, pregnancy-status, emirate/locale, language, household-role) — each tagged with what it drives (physiology · cohort stratification · UAE cut-points · localization). demographics_n > 0 auto-verifies.

Marker-side cold-start is handled — cohort-median fallback (Doc 01 §4.3) and the guideline→cohort→personal ignition model (Doc 14) — and a new user can now be resolved to a persona (F2, Appx I). But the question-side cold-start is undocumented: which minimal item set bootstraps day-0 scoring, the order items are surfaced, and how coverage/Confidence ramps as labs and wearables arrive. Fix: a progressive-profiling schedule — minimal first-run set → expand by leverage/persona.

Built (D26): the question-side cold-start is specified — a 7-item bootstrap set (PHQ-2, GAD-2, sleep, activity, AUDIT-C, smoking, diet) that seeds a day-0 score and resolves a persona, plus a progressive-profiling schedule (session-1 bootstrap → remaining bank by P1→P5 applicability → triggered deep-dives → cadence refresh). coldstart_items > 0 auto-verifies.

items.title: Consent & device-pairing not placed in the intake flow

versions.body: Consent/privacy is owned by Doc 11 and device surfaces + household accounts by Doc 18 §2/§4/§6, but neither sequences when consent is taken or what is gated until a wearable is paired during first-run. Fix: position consent capture and device-pairing as explicit, ordered onboarding steps with their gating rules.

Built (D26): consent & device-pairing are now ordered first-run steps with explicit gating — privacy consent (step 3) blocks all capture; device-pairing (step 8) gates wearable metrics/early-warning; EHR-connect (step 9) gates Patient360 corroboration; the actuarial layer stays firewalled/off by default. consent_gates > 0 auto-verifies.
